title: Apply Corollary 1: A diagonal divides a parallelogram into two congruent triangles
show: parallelogram ABCD with opposite angles (4x+10)° and (6x-20)° marked

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|\angle ABC| = (4x + 10)^\circ$ and $|\angle CDA| = (6x - 20)^\circ$. Find $x$ and $|\angle ABC|$.

steps.say: Draw the diagonal $[AC]$. By Corollary 1, triangles $ABC$ and $CDA$ are congruent.

rows.aside: $B$ in the first triangle matches $D$ in the second.

steps.say: In congruent triangles the matching angles are equal. $|\angle ABC|$ matches $|\angle CDA|$, so set them equal.
Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.
Put $x = 15$ into $|\angle ABC|$.

title: Apply Theorem 11: Three parallel lines cutting equal segments on one transversal cut equal segments on any
show: three parallel lines AD, BE, CF cutting two transversals with AB=BC and corresponding segments marked equal

example.question: The parallel lines $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ cut the transversal $[AC]$ with $|AB| = |BC|$. They cut the second transversal $[DF]$ at $D$, $E$ and $F$. $|DE| = (2x + 1)$ cm and $|EF| = (4x - 9)$ cm. Find $x$ and $|DF|$.

steps.say: Three parallel lines cut equal pieces $|AB| = |BC|$ on one transversal. By Theorem 11 they cut equal pieces on every transversal.
Put the two lengths equal to each other.
Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.
Find $|DE|$, then double it, since $|EF|$ is the same.

title: Apply Theorem 13: Similar triangles have proportional sides
show: two equiangular triangles ABC and DEF with sides 6, 9 and 8 cm matching

example.question: In the diagram, triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are equiangular. $|AB| = 6$ cm, $|BC| = 9$ cm and $|DE| = 8$ cm. $AB$ and $DE$ are opposite equal angles, and so are $BC$ and $EF$. Find $|EF|$.

steps.say: The triangles have equal angles, so they are similar (Theorem 13). $AB$ matches $DE$, and $BC$ matches $\hl{1}{EF}$.

rows.aside: Write the known pair first, then the pair with the unknown.

steps.say: Replace each length with its value. The unknown stays as $\hl{1}{|EF|}$.
Cross-multiply, then divide to leave $\hl{1}{|EF|}$ on its own.

title: Apply Theorem 21: Perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord; perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre
show: circle centre O, chord AB=24 cm, perpendicular OM to the chord bisecting it, right triangle OMA

example.question: A circle has centre $O$. A chord $[AB]$ has length $24$ cm. The perpendicular from $O$ meets $[AB]$ at $M$, and $|OM| = 5$ cm. Find the radius of the circle.

steps.say: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord (Theorem 21). So $M$ is the midpoint of $[AB]$.
Join $O$ to $A$. Then $OMA$ is a right-angled triangle with the right angle at $M$, and $|OA|$ is the radius $\hl{2}{r}$.
The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
The radius is a length, so take the positive root.

title: Find lengths using similar triangles
show: two similar triangles ABC and PQR with matching sides AB=8, PQ=14, AC=12 marked

example.question: Triangles $ABC$ and $PQR$ are similar. $|AB| = 8$ cm and $|PQ| = 14$ cm are matching sides. $|AC| = 12$ cm. Find $|PR|$, the side that matches $[AC]$.

steps.say: Divide a side of the bigger triangle by the matching side of the smaller one. This gives $\hl{1}{k}$, the number that turns $ABC$ into $PQR$.
$PR$ matches $AC$. Multiply $|AC|$ by the scale factor $\hl{1}{k}$.
$PQR$ is the bigger triangle, so $|PR|$ should be bigger than $|AC| = 12$. It is.

rows.aside: Always check that the bigger triangle gets the bigger answer.

title: Apply Theorem 12: A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two in the same ratio
show: triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC, D on AB, E on AC, |AD|=4, |DB|=6

example.question: In triangle $ABC$, $D$ is on $[AB]$ and $E$ is on $[AC]$. $DE$ is parallel to $BC$. $|AD| = 4$ cm, $|DB| = 6$ cm and $|AE| = 5$ cm. Find $|EC|$.

steps.say: $DE$ is parallel to $BC$, so it cuts $[AB]$ and $[AC]$ in the same ratio (Theorem 12).

rows.aside: Top and bottom must be in the same order on both sides.

steps.say: Replace each length with its value.
Cross-multiply, then divide by $4$ to leave $\hl{1}{|EC|}$ on its own.
